statement: How many integers $n$ satisfy the inequality $|3n - 4| \le 11$?

choices.misconception: I solved the inequality correctly but counted only the integers from $0$ to $5$, leaving out the negative integers $-2$ and $-1$ even though they also satisfy it.
I forgot to add $4$ to the left side, so I used $-11 \le 3n \le 15$, which allows $n = -3$ through $5$.
I treated the inequality as strict and left out $n = 5$, even though $|3(5) - 4| = 11$ satisfies $\le 11$.

hints: Solve $-11 \le 3n - 4 \le 11$ for $n$, then count the integers in that interval.

solutions.reliable: Rewrite as $-11 \le 3n - 4 \le 11$. Adding $4$ gives $-7 \le 3n \le 15$, and dividing by $3$ gives $-2.33\ldots \le n \le 5$. The integers in this interval are $-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5$, which is $8$ integers. Check the ends: $|3(-2) - 4| = 10 \le 11$ and $|3(5) - 4| = 11 \le 11$, while $|3(-3) - 4| = 13$ and $|3(6) - 4| = 14$ are too big.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
